html:
TON, TOF, RTO

A timer tag has a preset (.PRE, milliseconds), an accumulator (.ACC) and three bits: .EN (the rung is true), .TT (timing: true while the accumulator is climbing toward the preset) and .DN (done). TON(Dwell,1000,0) means: timer Dwell, preset 1000 ms, accumulator starts at 0.

InstructionBehaviour
TONOn-delay. Rung true: ACC counts up; at PRE, DN turns on. Rung false: ACC and DN reset. The ordinary “wait a second” timer.
TOFOff-delay. DN turns on the moment the rung is true and stays on for PRE after the rung goes false. A fan that runs on after the heater stops.
RTORetentive. Like TON but the accumulator holds when the rung goes false and resumes when it comes back; only RES clears it. Run-hour meters, cumulative faults.

The timer in Part IV’s step 2 is the heartbeat of the whole line:

XIC(Line_Run)XIO(Conv_Index)[RTO(Dwell,1000,0),OTE(Bottle_Feed_Emit)];

The rung is true whenever the line runs and the belt is not stepping, so the timer runs while the belt stands still. When Dwell.DN comes on, step 4 shifts the registers and step 3 steps the belt: Conv_Index goes true, the rung goes false, and step 3 resets the timer for the next stop (an RTO keeps its time until a RES clears it). The feeder’s Emit is on the same rung: the feeder is in edge mode, so it drops one bottle per stop.

A flasher is two timers chasing each other, or one timer that resets itself:

resets itself the scan after it finishes: DN is true for one scan every 500 ms
XIO(Flash.DN)TON(Flash,500,0);

An easier flasher to read is a pair: XIO(T_Off.DN)TON(T_On,500,0); XIC(T_On.DN)TON(T_Off,500,0); XIC(T_On.TT)OTE(Lamp);, on while T_On times and off while T_Off times. The sandbox’s lights and stack lights also have a When on setting (steady, flashing, fast flash, pulsing) that flashes for you, so the output only has to be on.

CTU, CTD, RES

A counter counts rung transitions, false to true, into .ACC; .DN comes on at .PRE. CTU(Boxes,10,0) counts up; CTD counts down; RES(Boxes) zeroes the accumulator (RES also resets timers). Because a counter has its own edge detection you do not need an ONS in front of it, but you do need the rung to go false between counts, which is why a counter fed by a sensor counts parts and a counter fed by a held button counts once.

Part IV keeps its counts with ADD behind a one-shot rather than CTU, for a reason worth knowing: the four displays show plain DINTs, the thumbwheel compares against a plain DINT, and a CTU’s accumulator is just a DINT inside a structure. Both are right; ADD keeps the tag list flat.

Try it

Build a belt with a photo-eye and a feeder set to automatic. Count the eye with XIC(PE_1_Detect)CTU(Parts,5,0); and light a lamp on Parts.DN; reset it with a button through RES. Then replace CTU with ONS(P_ONS)ADD(Count,1,Count) and show Count on a Digital Display.
